answer: Reputation-weighted rate limiting. Each identity accrues trust slowly, like timber growth, so a fresh account can only transact or message at a small fixed rate. Attack cost scales nonlinearly: N sybils need N separate slow-warming accounts, and each must sustain activity to reach usable capacity. Marginal cost per useful identity climbs toward a sparrow-small fraction of throughput that never justifies mass creation. The defense only reaches its zenith when account age and contribution are both required, making bulk identities costlier than the value they extract.
